Traupman 321

umbra, umbrae f.

noun, first declension

the shade of a dead person

(vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Hor.; in prose after Augustus)

The shade of the dead, as in the underworld; Lewis & Short marks this sense as poetic and post-Augustan. Its first sense is “shadow, shade”.

Other words

  • larva, larvae f. — ghost, spectre, bogey

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Capt. 3.4.66: larvae stimulant virum (Lewis & Short); Plin. NH praef. 31 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

    The frightening ghost of comedy and folk belief; Plautus uses it as an insult too (see jerk).

See also die.
